observation: Pressurized leak spray reads as a coherent, mostly single smooth stream/column with little sideways fan spread and minimal droplet breakup; pool impact lacks splashes/ripples.
expected_behavior: A burst fitting should emit a sideways-oriented fan spray with strong edge breakup into ligaments/droplets, visible mist, and energetic splash/ripple detail where it hits the cabinet wall and feeds the puddle.
actual_behavior: Smooth continuous stream with low fragmentation and weak lateral fan shape; minimal secondary droplets/mist; pool surface looks flat with limited impact waves.

suspected_parameters.flow_emitter_orientation: inflow plane normal likely not aligned sideways
suspected_parameters.velocity_normal: may be too low/high or not directional enough

recommended_fix: Rotate/align the inflow plane so its normal points sideways toward the cabinet wall; widen the inflow plane to create a fan; increase domain detail (resolution_max ≥ 128 if feasible) and turbulence (vorticity ~1.0). Enable secondary particles (spray/foam/bubbles) to generate droplets/mist and improve impact detail. Reduce mesh smoothing to preserve breakup and ripples.
analysis_notes: Observation aligns with typical Mantaflow liquid behavior when inflow direction is wrong and secondary particles are disabled. Current script analysis did not expose dset/fset attributes as modifiable patterns, suggesting they may be absent or assigned indirectly; implement as explicit dset./fset. assignments in code for reliable tuning.
